caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.630 of 1998
lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Attorney-General, instructed by Md Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record— For the Petitioners.
Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record — For the Respondents.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md Abdul Malek Miah and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 2. The respondents instituted the above Administrative Tribunal case stating that in pursuance of some advertisements inviting applications for appointment as Steno-Typists they submitted applications, sat for practical test on 6-11-93 and having been successful were appointed to the said post by the Superintendent of Police, Kurigram, opposite party No. 7 in the Administrative Tribunal Case on 28-2-94. They joined their duties. While they were working as such the said office by an order dated 17-7-94 cancelled their appointments and directed them to return within 15 days the money they received as pay and allowances. Under the instruction of Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Rajshahi Division (who was opposite Party No.5 in the Administrative Tribunal Case) a direction was given to take steps for the respondents' appointments through the Divisional Selection Board. In response thereto the said Superintendent of Police, Kurigram addressed the Commissioner, Rajshahi Division, opposite the appointments in question made without approval of the Divisional Selection Board was valid and lawful. He submits that the power of appointment of the Superintendent of Police was conditional upon prior approval, of the Divisional Selection Board, in accordance with the Circular dated 28-7-76, but the Appellate Tribunal was wrong in not holding that the appointments made by the Superintendent of Police without prior approval of the Divisional Selection Board was incompetent and without lawful authority. He submits that the petitioners ''do not insist upon the respondents'' cessation of service by the impugned order dated 17-7-94 but they are aggrieved by the observations of the Appellate Tribunal that the Circular dated 28-4-76 was only for executive guidance having no statutory force. The learned Attorney-General has placed reliance on the case of Bangladesh vs Shafiuddin Ahmed, 50 DLR (AD) 17 in support of his submission that a Circular of general application with sufficient details emanating from the rule-making authority has the force of statute party No.3 in the Administrative Tribunal case, on 29-9-94 for regularization of the respondents'' appointments through the said Divisional Selection Board. Thereafter, the respondents submitted representations to the Home Minister who on 26-12-94 directed regularization of their appointments after correcting the mistake. Thereupon the Inspector-General of Police by his Memo, dated 4-1-95 addressed the said opposite party Nos. 3 and 5-7 informing them about the Minister''s direction. In the meantime the Deputy Commissioner, Unigram, opposite party No. 6 in the Administrative Tribunal Case, by his Memo dated 28-12-94 informed the said opposite party No. 7 that the Divisional Selection Board refused to consider the matter. The respondents waited for some time and as no action was taken by the authority they instituted Administrative Tribunal Case No. 70 of 1995 before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra which by order dated 28-6-95 rejected the application for want of cause of action on the ground that it was premature. Thereafter the respondents submitted a representation to the said opposite party No. 3. The matter was discussed on 15-10-95 at a meeting of the Divisional Selection Board and by Memo dated 7-12-95 the Secretary, Establishment Division, opposite party No.2 in the Administrative Tribunal case, informed the respondents that there was no scope for their re-instatement and the Board accordingly, rejected their representation. Thereafter, the instant Administrative Tribunal Case No.128 of 1995 was filed on 23-12-95 on the allegations, inter alia, that the impugned order dated 17-7-94 passed by the Superintendent of Police, Kurigram cancelling their appointments had been passed without giving them an opportunity of being heard.
